speaker: stephanieasher
text: Council acknowledges the Wadawurrung, traditional owners of this land, and I pay my respects to all Elders, past and present, and to all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people who are part of the Greater Geelong community today. This meeting's being held virtually, as is fairly obvious, and the recording of the meeting will be published on the Council's website. So good evening, everybody, and thank you for tuning in with Election Day on Saturday. Tonight is actually the final meeting of this Council as a group, and we're glad to be sharing it with the community via the livestream. This was something that we introduced three years ago, so it's fantastic that it's actually happened. Now, we are in caretaker mode, so this meeting will be short and straight to the point. It's been an honour for us all to represent you during the past three years, and a particular privilege for me personally to serve you as Mayor for the last 12 months. Now, the purpose of tonight's meeting is to consider the City of Greater Geelong's 2019 to 20 annual report, and I'm sure all the Councillors will be looking forward to reflecting on some of the achievements that it details. Before we do that, I will take the opportunity to say a big thanks to my 10 Councillor colleagues for your hard work, your dedication, the time you spend every day, every week, 24-7, we all know that, and also for your dedication and leadership during the whole term of office. Thanks also to the City's CEO, Martin Cutter, the executive leadership team, and all the staff who have worked very hard to implement our decisions, put up with our persistent nagging, and carry out the actions in our strategic plans during the past three years. So, thanks again, everybody. And with that, let's begin the final meeting. Now, firstly, Councillor Murray, here's an unfortunate apology for tonight's meeting. Do we have any other apologies to note? I don't think we do. Are there any declarations of conflict of interest for tonight's agenda? I don't think there will be. And we need to confirm some minutes, so may I please have a mover and seconder to confirm the minutes of the Ordinary Council Meeting held on the 21st of September, 2020? Moved by Councillor Grisbeck, seconded by Councillor Mansfield. Thank you. All those in favour? Those against? Carried. Thank you. Okay, so section B reports only has the one item, which is the City of Greater Geelong Annual Report 2019-2020 to be moved by Councillor Aitken, and seconded by Councillor Grisbeck. Councillor Aitken.

speaker: anthonyaitken
text: Thank you very much, Mayor Ashton. It's my pleasure to move the following recommendation that Council notes the Annual Report and the Annual Report Summary. This is a statutory requirement of local government. In fact, most businesses as well, too, have to produce an annual report. Well, Council does as well, too. This document actually outlines our achievements for the 19-20 financial year, and also our financial position. A number of items have already been discussed in the media in terms of reporting on this particular document, but I'd actually just like to highlight some other areas that haven't received as much attention. The first I want to do is to acknowledge that in 19-20, this Council continued to implement its transparency about the historic culture and bullying that existed in the City of Greater Geelong. We took significant steps in 19-20 to actually announce a more transparent and open discussion on that particular issue, and I want to congratulate Martin Cutter for doing that in particular. We also put significant additional resources into our planning and engineering section of the City of Greater Geelong, and that we are now seeing a much more customer-focused, and also from a planning perspective, we're actually now starting to see a reduction in some of the timeframes that were associated there. That was actually a significant investment of this particular Council during that particular year. We continued to implement the Commission of Inquiries Transformation Plan, and successfully we met all the requirements associated with that. In 19-20, we also made the final decision to create the new City Accommodation Building in the CBD of Geelong. Some of the significant policy positions and strategy decisions that Council made during 19-20 included the Sustainability Framework. One I'm personally very proud of, which is the Social Housing Plan for 2020 to 2041. A personal one that has taken a long time, but we've finally done that, is the Reconciliation Action Plan. Another major achievement that I actually like, if you look in the annual report, there was perfect attendance at the meetings by the Windermere Ward Councillors. So the community should be very proud of what their two representatives have achieved there. Perfect attendance. And on a personal note again, what a major achievement 12 months ago during 19-20, when this particular Council elected the first ever female leadership team in the City of Greater Geelong. That was a huge achievement during 19-20. And not only the first leadership team, it was only the second time ever that a female had been elected into the leadership role as Mayor of the City of Greater Geelong. They are major achievements that were achieved by this Council during the 19-20 financial year. We do have challenges and they continue to put us under pressure. They include the financial constraints that we're operating under in the local government sector. Rate capping at CPI is making difficult for organisations like the City of Greater Geelong. And of course, COVID was a significant financial and continues to be a significant financial challenge for the organisation. And we will see that in the 2021 financial year as well too. We continue the battle between asset maintenance and asset renewal and new assets. Unfortunately, there isn't an easy mix to this particular challenge that the Council has. The rejuvenation in our existing area is under pressure, but so is the provision of new services and new infrastructure in the parts of the community that are growing significantly within the City of Greater Geelong. And the last comment that I wish to make on is that if you have a look in the 19-20 report, it's the first time that we've actually had some significant steps in addressing social inequality challenge that exists in the City of Greater Geelong. We made significant financial contributions to Geelong food relief, and we actually started some significant policy pieces in terms of social infrastructure. I think 19-20 was a fantastic year for this Council, and the annual report actually says that. I'll make further comment in my closing about the financial position of the City of Greater Geelong.

There was some $122 million expended on capital expenditure in this last financial year, with 40% going to roads and footpaths. Going into the next financial year, that's up to about $160 million of investment into capital expenditure, and that all relates to not only improving our infrastructure, such as vital roads and footpaths and drainage, but also creates real employment opportunities directly and indirectly through contractors and the like. So I'm really pleased with the work that we continue to do there, and next financial year, beyond the one we're in, is upping the capital expenditure once again. So I'm pleased with that. Equally, whilst we've got some work to do in areas of the environment and meeting our targets, we have measures in place that will allow us to achieve those targets, particularly through the guidance of our sustainability framework and our environmental plan from 22 to 30. And it's pleasing to see that we've planted some 3,255 odd trees in our parks and gardens. Personally, I'm really pleased with two initiatives that we've introduced that really has put money back into the community's pockets. One is the hard waste collection that this council adopted has been extremely well-received, and I know that community are extremely pleased with that. There's been some 15,000 odd hard waste collections. And of course, the free CBD parking has been extremely well-received, and I'm really proud that this council has achieved that. Lastly, the one area that I'd like to highlight that we need to work a lot more on and needs to be our number one priority going forward, and that's the health and safety of our employees and the people that work for the organisation. It is pleasing that our LTI rates have come down and that they're down from the previous financial year to some 18% LTI from the previous 27. It's also pleasing that our hypo incidents are down. That's been a significant decrease, but TRIFA is still up, and it must remain the focus for this organisation, regardless of who the council is going forward, and regardless of what senior executive looks like going forward. The health and safety of our employees must be the number one priority and the number one focus of this organisation into the immediate, medium, and long-term future.
